preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the tree is between 1 and 50 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= ui <= n and 1 <= vi <= n and 1 <= wi <= 50 for ui, vi, wi in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two vertices in the range [1, n] and has a length between 1 and 50 (inclusive). The graph is a tree (connected and acyclic).
The starting vertex of the policeman, s, is within the valid vertex range.
The number of criminals, m, is between 1 and 50 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= xj <= n and xj != s for xj in criminals)
preconditions.description: Each criminal's starting vertex xj is within the valid vertex range and distinct from the policeman's starting vertex s.
The list of criminals contains exactly m vertices.

postconditions.description: The output is either 'Terrorists win' (if the policeman cannot catch all criminals) or a non-negative integer representing the minimal time required to catch all criminals under optimal behavior.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'Terrorists win' or (stdout.isdigit() and int(stdout) == min_time)
postconditions.description: If the policeman can catch all criminals, the output is the minimal time required, where min_time is the smallest T such that there exists a path for the policeman to visit all criminals' positions (accounting for their optimal movement) within time T.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'Terrorists win' if any(xj == s for xj in criminals) else True
postconditions.description: The output is 'Terrorists win' if and only if there exists at least one criminal already at the policeman's starting vertex s (though P5 already ensures this cannot happen).

postconditions.expression: stdout != 'Terrorists win' if all_possible_paths_exist else False
postconditions.description: The output is not 'Terrorists win' if and only if there exists a sequence of vertices (including s) such that the policeman can traverse the tree to catch all criminals optimally, accounting for their arbitrary-speed movement.
